Title: Choose the Good
Source Situation / Theme: An isolated mountain childhood; fear of government and school; a father interprets scripture as absolute instruction; a grandmother quietly offers another path.
Design Extraction: The mountain is both home and boundary. Authority controls information, while curiosity first appears as the possibility of leaving.
Game Transformation: Open with chores at the compound, a school bus passing below, and a private offer to follow a road the player has been told to fear.
Guardrail: Keep the emotional structure, not the exact Ruby Ridge story or Westover dialogue.

Title: The Midwife
Source Situation / Theme: Mother becomes a midwife and herbal healer, gains skill and income, and helps secure records that the children lack.
Design Extraction: Care can create competence and independence, yet it can also keep a closed system functioning without outside help.
Game Transformation: Build the Herb House as a care-and-crafting hub where the player treats people, prepares remedies, and chooses whether to document outcomes.
Guardrail: Do not turn childbirth or medical risk into a score-chasing minigame.

Title: Cream Shoes
Source Situation / Theme: Tara reconstructs her mother's orderly upbringing, rebellious marriage, and growing separation from her maternal family.
Design Extraction: Family identity is made from stories, objects, class differences, and choices that later generations inherit.
Game Transformation: Turn old photographs, clothing, letters, and town landmarks into an optional family-history investigation with competing accounts.
Guardrail: Use invented family history and objects; avoid duplicating identifiable biographies.

Title: Apache Women
Source Situation / Theme: A trip meant to relieve the father's depression ends in a severe car crash, a brain injury, and later disagreement about cause and blame.
Design Extraction: Danger emerges from many choices, and memory can preserve fragments while changing the meaning of an event.
Game Transformation: Create a road-trip sequence with fatigue, weather, seat-belt, and route decisions, followed by a memory-journal reconstruction.
Guardrail: Transform the crash circumstances; never reward reckless driving or graphic injury.

Title: Honest Dirt
Source Situation / Theme: Tyler leaves for college; his love of order, music, and study shows Tara a different way of living. Tara also encounters ordinary hygiene expectations.
Design Extraction: A new future often appears first through another person's habits, not through a speech.
Game Transformation: Jonah's departure leaves behind books, recordings, tools, and an unfinished application that quietly expand Mara's possible actions.
Guardrail: Avoid mocking rural poverty or treating hygiene differences as comic spectacle.

Title: Shield and Buckler
Source Situation / Theme: Tara and Richard enter dangerous scrapyard labor; an injury and fear awaken her wish to attend school, but she backs down.
Design Extraction: Competence can grow inside unsafe systems. Speaking a desire aloud may be a bigger risk than the physical task.
Game Transformation: Use the cracked-axle repair as the core tutorial: careful method, risky shortcut, asking for help, or stopping work.
Guardrail: The player may choose safety without losing the story or being shamed by the game.

Title: The Lord Will Provide
Source Situation / Theme: Luke is badly burned; Tara responds alone; the family relies on herbs and prayer, and later memories conflict over who stopped the fire.
Design Extraction: Emergency action, faith, care, and memory can become one story even when the evidence does not fully agree.
Game Transformation: Stage a non-repeatable fire emergency followed by treatment choices and a journal entry separating what Mara saw, heard, and concluded.
Guardrail: No graphic spectacle, fail-state farming, or repeated trauma challenge.
